answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can admit newcomers through a metered river of entries. Each epoch, new keys enter one at a time and the entry fee doubles with every admission, resetting next epoch. An honest newcomer pays the base fee once; a farm pushing n clones through one epoch pays about 2^n, and spreading them out wins at most one cheap slot per epoch against rival entrants. Bids stay sealed under a cipher until the beacon opens them, so no one can time the queue. Fees sit in a willow escrow refunded after five passed answers, so only fakes lose them. Vouched keys skip spikes.
